newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS: In Danny's wake, U.S. oil companies reopen.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS: In Danny's wake, U.S. oil companies reopen.

text.p: As Hurricane Danny moved slowly away from New Orleans, oil companies in the region began restarting operations Friday.

The Louisiana Offshort Oil Port (LOOP), expects to have offshore operations back to normal on Saturday. One ship was scheduled was to offload crude Friday, though that has been delayed until the facility is returned to operation.

Texaco Inc said workers had been returning to offshore platforms and on-shore sites all day. All 365 workers evacuated should be back to work by Saturday and production had restarted though the facilities were not yet at full strength.
About 40,000 barrels of oil and 200 million cubic feet of natural gas per day were affected, the company said.
Chevron Corp said the storm was tracking "dead on" for its 295,000 barrel per day refinery in Pascagoula, Mississippi, which was shut earlier Friday as precautionary measure
Chevron said full oil and gas production in the Gulf was gradually returning to normal Friday, with current production running at 10 percent of the normal 125,000 bpd.
Shell Oil shut its 74,000 bpd refinery in Saraland, Alabama Friday, a spokesman there said. The refinery could be restarted Saturday evening if no power outages occur there, the source said.

Mobil Corp expected production would be back up by the weekend at six offshore fields shut Thursday. Those fields included Eugene Island 240, Green Canyon 18/60, Ship Shoal 72, Ship Shoal 182 and Main Pass fields 6/103 and 73.

Exxon Corp said it had suffered modest production losses at its onshore Grand Isle, Louisiana facilities, and that its 432,000 barrel per day Baton Rouge refinery had taken precautionary measures but operations there were unaffected.

The National Weather service said a hurricane warning remains in effect from Grand Isle, Louisiana to Destin, Florida, excluding New Orleans. At 4 pm cdt (2100 GMT), the center of Hurricane Danny was located near latitude 29.9 north and longitude 88.8 west, or about 65 miles (100 km) south-southwest of Mobile, Alabama.

Danny is moving slowly toward the northeast at 6 mph (9 km) and hour. The center is expected to hit the coast near the Alabama/Mississippi border Saturday morning. Maximum sustained winds are near 75 mph (120 KMH).
